newsitem.title: USA: U.S. budget negotiators report some progress.
newsitem.headline: U.S. budget negotiators report some progress.

text.p: White House and congressional budget negotiators reported some progress Monday towards agreement on domestic spending cuts in areas outside the politically sensitive health care programmes.

Senate Budget Committee chairman Pete Domenici told reporters, "We came to some tentative conclusions," and said talks would resume Tuesday. White House budget director Frank Raines said they had made progress in their quest for a balanced budget agreement. "Our exploration of differences has turned to an exploration of agreement," he said.

Domenici, a New Mexico Republican, said, "We're talking about 45 to 55 billions of dollars that we are close to agreement on, savings in mandatories (mandatory government spending) that are not Medicare, not Social Security, not Medicaid."

Democratic Sen. Frank Lautenberg, N.J, and his House counterpart Representative John Spratt, S.C, said they were more optimistic but questioned whether a final agreement could be ready to take to Republican congressional leaders and President Clinton by Friday.

Domenici has said he would give the budget negotiations until Friday to make significant progress on a plan to balance the budget by 2002 and give taxpayers a tax cut, or he will start working for an agreement without the White House.

"I remain pretty committed to the proposition that we've got about a week, and after the week, if we don't get it done, I think we go another route, go without the president and try to put a bipartisan budget together up here," he said as the talks opened Monday.
